name: Stifel Financial Corp.
sector: Finance — Wealth management / broker-dealer & investment banking
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow finance moat: a durable, advisor-centric wealth franchise — record total client assets of $580.1B at Q2 2026 (+12% YoY, company release), fee-based client assets of $224.5B at end-2025 (+16%), Global Wealth Management net revenue of $3.54B in FY2025, the #1 ranking in J.D. Power employee advisor satisfaction for four straight years, and a diversified second engine in the Institutional Group ($1.91B FY2025 net revenue incl. KBW investment banking) — with measured returns above the cost of capital (fundamentals.json roic_proxy 15.6% in 2022, 17.1% in 2023, 20.0% in 2024; non-GAAP ROTCE ~25% in FY2025 and 23.6% in Q2 2026) — against the structural limits of the model: advisors are portable and own the client relationship, revenue is geared to equity-market levels and policy rates, investment banking is deal-cycle cyclical, GAAP ROE is only 9.9%-12.9% over 2023-2025, and the Roberts structured-products supervision cases (a $180.0M legal provision in Q1 2025, with related cases still open) show a controls/franchise risk larger rivals do not currently carry. No network effect or hard switching-cost lock-in supports a score above the moderate band.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.2%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 8.10 vs 3-yr median 2.71 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.3x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
BIG_NET_CASH: net cash is 3.5x normalized OE — part of the price is a cash pile, not the operating business; note it in the verdict
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (9.0%) vs bull-case tier C (14.8%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Diversified wealth/investment-banking franchise, moat 5/10 — the engine's OCF base is broker/bank balance-sheet plumbing on a pre-split share basis; on the corrected maintenance-earnings base of $4.21/share (post-split) the $67.56 price yields an 11.70% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $48.43, so it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$48 (~$39 with a margin of safety).
moat_for: Advisor-centric wealth franchise at scale: record total client assets $580.1B at Q2 2026 (+12% YoY); fee-based client assets $224.5B at end-2025 (+16%) — recurring asset-based revenue
Advisor recruiting engine and culture: #1 in J.D. Power employee advisor satisfaction four straight years (company release); 181 advisors added in 2025
Diversified second engine: Institutional Group net revenue $1.91B in FY2025 (+20%), investment banking revenue +42% YoY in Q2 2026 — wealth + capital markets dampen any single cycle

Returns above cost of capital through the cycle: roic_proxy 15.6%/17.1%/20.0% (2022/2023/2024, fundamentals.json); non-GAAP ROTCE ~25% FY2025, 23.6% Q2 2026; OE positive 5 of last 5 FY on both definitions
moat_against: Advisors can leave and take clients with them; recruiting is an arms race (forgivable loans, transition packages) against Morgan Stanley, Schwab, Fidelity and large RIAs
Revenue geared to exogenous variables: asset-based fees ride equity-market levels; bank/sweep net interest income rides policy rates and deposit mix
Investment banking and transactional revenue are deal-cycle cyclical — the Institutional Group has no recurring-revenue floor comparable to wealth fees

Supervision/legal overhang: the Roberts structured-products cases forced a $180.0M provision in Q1 2025 (a $1.16/share pre-split EPS hit) and related claims are still being litigated — a franchise-controls risk, not just a cost line
